graders.evidence:
# UI Audit — Reminders (2026-10-30) ## Stack - Framework: Vanilla JS + FastAPI serving one Jinja2 template (`app/templates/index.html`) - Build tool: none - CSS: plain CSS in `app/static/styles.css`, plus inline `style=` attributes in the template - State: none (the server holds an in-memory list; the page re-fetches and re-renders after each change) - Design tokens: `app/static/styles.css` (`:root` block with 4 variables) - Run: `uvicorn app.main:app --reload` (run from the project root; inferred from `app/main.py` and `requirements.txt`, no README or Procfile) → http://127.0.0.1:8000 ## Pages / Routes (top 10) Single-page app: one route, three tabs switched client-side. - `/` — `app/templates/index.html` (route in `app/main.py`) - Tab "Today" (`#today`) — not-done reminders - Tab "All reminders" (`#all`) — every reminder - Tab "Settings" (`#settings`) — notification time field and Save button - `/api/reminders` (GET) — `app/main.py` - `/api/reminders/{id}/done` (POST) — `app/main.py` Components: no component files. Largest file is 35 lines, so no oversized-file issues (nothing over 500 lines). ## Style approach Styling is split between a small stylesheet and inline `style=` attributes on the body, header, tabs, views and settings form. A `:root` token block exists, but nothing uses it (0 `var(--` references); every color is a hard-coded hex, about 19 unique values, mostly near-duplicate blues and grays. ## Pain points ### 🔴 High - Not responsive: `` is fixed at `width: 800px`, `.view` at 760px, the input at 300px. There is no `` and no media queries, so it breaks on phones. - Tokens exist but are unused: `--color-primary`, `--color-success` etc. are defined, yet the same colors are repeated as raw hex (`#2b6cb0`, `#38a169`) inline and in the CSS. This is the highest-leverage fix for a redesign. - Broken, inaccessible logo: `` has no `alt`, and `logo.png` does not exist in `app/static/`, so it renders as a broken image. - Unescaped text injected with `innerHTML` (`app/static/app.js`): reminder titles are inserted as raw HTML, so a title containing markup would break the layout or run script. Must be kept in mind when porting the design. - Settings does nothing real: Save only shows a browser `alert()`; there is no backend endpoint for the notification time. The design must not promise it works. ### 🟡 Medium - No loading state: both `fetch` calls (`loadReminders`, `markDone`) have no spinner, skeleton or disabled button, and no error handling. - Tabs lack semantics and feedback: no active-tab highlight, no `role="tablist"`/`aria-selected`, no `aria-` attributes at all; no `

graders.name: report-content
graders.evidence:
# UI Audit — Reminders (2026-10-30) ## Stack - Framework: Vanilla JS + FastAPI serving one Jinja template - Build tool: none - CSS: plain CSS in `app/static/styles.css`, plus inline `style=` in the template - State: none (DOM is re-rendered from `/api/reminders` after each action) - Design tokens: `app/static/styles.css` (`:root` with 4 variables) - Run: `uvicorn app.main:app` from the project root → http://127.0.0.1:8000 (inferred from the entry point; no README or script confirms it) ## Pages / Routes (top 10) Single-page app: one template, three client-side tabs. - `/` — `app/templates/index.html` (page shell, "Hello {{ owner }}" header) - Tab "Today" — `#today` in `app/templates/index.html`, filled by `app/static/app.js` - Tab "All reminders" — `#all`, filled by `app/static/app.js` - Tab "Settings" — `#settings` (notification time field) - `/api/reminders` — `app/main.py` (GET, data only) - `/api/reminders/{id}/done` — `app/main.py` (POST, data only) Size: 3 front-end files (`index.html` 26, `app.js` 35, `styles.css` 13 lines). Nothing is above 500 lines. ## Style approach Styling is split between a tiny stylesheet and inline `style=` attributes (11 in the template). The stylesheet defines 4 design tokens, but nothing uses them; every colour is a raw hex value (about 17 unique). The page is a fixed 800px column. ## Pain points ### 🔴 High - **Not responsive:** `body` is fixed at `width: 800px`, `.view` at `760px`, and the Settings input at `300px`. There is no `` and no media queries, so the page breaks on phones. - **Tokens exist but are unused:** `--color-primary`, `--color-success`, `--color-text` and `--space-2` are defined but never referenced. The same blue and green are repeated as hex in inline styles and CSS, along with greys such as #333, #444 and #555. This is the highest-leverage fix for a redesign. - **Broken logo and no accessibility basics:** `/static/logo.png` does not exist (the file is missing from `app/static`). The `` also has no `alt`. The page has no `lang` attribute and no `
`, `
` or `
`. Tabs are plain buttons with no `role="tab"` or `aria-selected`, and the active tab is never highlighted. - **Unsafe rendering:** `app.js` inserts `r.title` into `innerHTML` without escaping, so a reminder title containing HTML would run as markup. Developer attention is needed before the design port. ### 🟡 Medium - **No loading, empty or error states:** the two `fetch` calls (list, mark done) show nothing while waiting or on failure. An empty list is a blank area (the `.empty` class exists but is never used). - **Settings does not save:** the Save button only shows an `alert()`. The backend has no settings endpoint, and the time input has no label or type. The design port must not promise a working Settings screen. - **"Today" is not by date:** it lists every not-done reminder, regardless of its due date. - **Inline style sprawl:** 11 `style=` attributes in a 26-line template (below the 50 threshold, but they override the stylesheet). ### 🟢 Low - **Small tap targets and no focus styling:** buttons use `6px 10px` padding, and the Done button remains on completed items. - **Hardcoded English text:** there are no i18n markers. This matters only if more languages are planned. - **Alerts and `onclick=` attributes:** these are inline handlers and a browser `alert()`. They are worth replacing during the port, but they are not blocking. ## Recommendation Confirm scenario C: the app is tiny, the stack is simple, and a visual port into the existing template and stylesheet is quick. Tell the designer that Settings has no backend, and fix the unescaped `innerHTML` first.
